T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based framework to design an intuitive and responsive interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems.
T1.notes: Focus on user experience and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a normalized schema to store problem details, tags, difficulty levels, and metadata.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a code editor interface with syntax highlighting, auto-completion, and error highlighting.
T4.notes: Ensure compatibility with multiple programming languages.

T5.implementation_approach: Connect the code editor UI with the backend to send code for execution and display results.
T5.notes: Handle asynchronous communication and error states.

T6.implementation_approach: Set up a secure and isolated environment (e.g., Docker containers) to execute user-submitted code.
T6.notes: Ensure security and resource limits to prevent abuse.

T7.implementation_approach: Implement logic to compare user-submitted outputs with expected outputs and handle edge cases.

T8.implementation_approach: Design a user profile page to display user details, activity history, and achievements.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user data, including profile updates and retrieval.
T9.notes: Ensure secure handling of sensitive user data.

T10.implementation_approach: Design a schema to store user information, preferences, and activity logs.
T10.notes: Ensure compliance with data privacy regulations.

T11.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface to display user rankings and scores.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data based on user performance.

T13.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and explanations for problems.
T13.notes: Ensure hints are displayed progressively to avoid spoilers.

T14.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and explanations for problems.
T14.notes: Allow for versioning of hints and explanations.

T15.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the problem library.
T15.notes: Focus on edge cases and performance.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the code editor and online judge for correctness, performance, and security.

T17.implementation_approach: Test user profiles and leaderboard functionality for accuracy and responsiveness.
T17.notes: Ensure data consistency and real-time updates.

T18.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using cloud services and CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy
db = SQLAlchemy()

def init_db(app):
    """
    Initialize the database with the given Flask application.
    """
    db.init_app(app)
    with app.app_context():
        # Create all tables if they don't exist
        db.create_all()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    input_format = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    output_format = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    constraints = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    examples = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.title}>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    result = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)

    user = db.relationship('User', back_populates='solutions')
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', back_populates='solutions')

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id} language={self.language} result={self.result}>"

# app/routes.py

# Required Imports
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Registers all blueprints to the given Flask app instance.

    Args:
        app (Flask): The Flask application instance.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint)

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    
    # Configure the app (example configuration, adjust as needed)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///acm_platform.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)
    
    # Register blueprints
    register_blueprints(app)
    
    return app

from app import create_app

# Entry point for the ACM Problem-Solving Platform
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = create_app()
    app.run(debug=True)

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Editor: An integrated code editor with support for multiple programming languages.
- Online Judge: An automated system to evaluate submitted solutions and provide feedback.
- User Profiles: Profiles for users to track their progress, achievements, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: A leaderboard to display top-performing users based on problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Explanations: Optional hints and detailed explanations for problems to aid learning.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
